roles.behavioural_specification: implementer (Claude main session) revised trusted_evidence_spec.md for 005-W: 고르는 질문 표시 (choice_codes on the first call, contract v17), spec 4; status-code letter is not the pronoun I, spec 2
roles.acceptance_construction: a separate agent that read only trusted_evidence_spec.md and an earlier suite (for format), per the suite's own about text
roles.expected_result_review: a further separate agent that read only trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-W), the 005-W suite and the 005-V review (for format). No .py file in the repository, runs/, benchmarks/, notebooks, tests, the author's scratch folder or other suites were opened and no repository code was run. The suite was split (split.py) into inputs.json and a sealed file (rationale, expected); admission decisions and reasons, pre_inference, uncovered_items, statuses incl. split parts, reply language, must_cite, end_to_end and polarity were derived by hand from the inputs (derive.py, derivation_blind.json) before the sealed file was opened; asked/covered items were re-checked by an item-table script (items.py) and the choice/conflict/code-letter rules by focus.py.

independence_limit: All roles are instances of the same model family in one session. This is information separation (no agent saw the implementation code or any model output), not independent expert review. The 'rule' and 'category' labels (e.g. 'choice_vi_reentry_processing_right_code_first', 'conflict_template_…', 'choice_near_miss_…') and the suite's 'about' text (which names the six choice cases and three near-misses) were visible during derivation and may have primed it; the choice and conflict sets were nonetheless recomputed mechanically from the spec rules.
review_result: Blind derivation agreed with the suite in 81/81 cases on every spec-derived field (admission ids and reasons, pre_inference, uncovered_items, model_statuses incl. split parts, expected_language, must_cite, end_to_end, expected_polarity). choice_codes (spec 4, 005-W) fall on exactly 02, 45, 62, 68, 70, 81 (in question order: [I-5-2,I-5-4], [I-5-3,I-5-1], [I-5-1,I-5-2], [I-5-3,I-5-4], [I-5-1,I-5-4], [I-5-2,I-5-3]); near-misses 18 (I-5-2 with its parent I-5), 58 (H-9 never named by admissible evidence, one named code), 60 (no choosing word) get none. Number-only conflict pairs fall on exactly 28, 29, 30, 44, 56, 59, 67 (once status codes are kept verbatim; a naive digit mask would wrongly pair 33, 79, 80). No question becomes personal only through the I of I-5-x; the only real first-person English questions are 35 (personal) and 42 (no judgment request). The 275-answer bank found 39 misjudgements on the suite (1 correct failing, 38 wrong passing) and 14 after the proposed 19 edits in 17 cases (0 correct failing; 13 value swaps between codes that no non-binding pattern can see, and the 'ảnh' substring gap in 33).

focus_005w.choice_codes_rule: codes = status-code tokens of the question after removing a document_id found in it (spec 2/5); choosing words of spec 5 ('or','which','hay','hoặc' word-bounded; Korean phrases and 'nào' as substrings); drop codes in a parent/child pair; choice question if two or more remain and a choosing word is present; choice_codes = remaining codes written in the part's admissible text, in question order, only if two or more (spec 4, 005-W).

near_misses.A05W-18: I-5-2 and its parent I-5 with 'hay': parent/child pair, no codes left; no choice_codes, no retry
near_misses.A05W-58: I-5-4/H-9 with 'or' is a choice question (different families), but admissible evidence names only I-5-4: fewer than two named codes, so no choice_codes and no retry reachable; question code I-5-4
near_misses.A05W-60: I-5-1/I-5-3 siblings without a choosing word ('각각'): not a choice question
near_misses.others: 10 ('which'), 64 ('nào') have one code; 28 and 44 have 'I-5' (from 'I-5 stay booklet') plus one sub-code, a parent/child pair; 57 and 73 lose 'I-5' with the removed document name. Substring 'or' (for, foreigner, report, work) hits 24 questions but changes no outcome; 'thay' occurs in no two-code question.

focus_005w.conflict_records_rule: pairs of admissible records in the same part whose text, after removing the leading [title], is equal once every number (outside status codes) is masked and differs as written (spec 4, 005-U; spec 5).

conflict_near_misses.A05W-31: same value in both records: identical text, no pair
conflict_near_misses.A05W-33: I-5-1/I-5-4 fee records differ only by code: not a pair because codes are kept
conflict_near_misses.A05W-79/80: sub-code records differ only by code and are in separate parts anyway

focus_005w.status_code_letter_I: With codes masked, only 35 ('I hold … Am I allowed') and 42 ('told me … I am a little uneasy') contain a real English first person. English questions with a judgment word and an I-5 code (01, 14, 37, 58, 62, 72, 10) would read as personal if the I of I-5-x counted; none of them has records that branch on a missing fact, so pre_inference would not change, but 73 and 80 split only because they are general, and they remain general under either reading (no judgment word). The rule is therefore satisfied by the suite but exercised only weakly: no case would flip its pre_inference or split under the wrong reading.

defects_found.what: Wrong answers that ban the museum work outright but mention the 14-hour figure pass ('… cannot take part-time work as a museum guide, even for 14 hours a week'; 'No, the manual mentions a 14-hour week but … cannot work as a guide'). 'can' also matches inside 'cannot', so group 0 is satisfied.
defects_found.why: The skip look-ahead of pattern 0 counts any hour figure ((?:\d+|ten|fourteen) hours) as a cap, in both the sentence branch and the bare-'No' branch; the cap form of spec 5 (005-S) is a negation plus a cap word before the number, which the other skip words already cover. Same gap the 005-V review fixed in 01/03/37.
defects_found.effect: both wrong answers fire; all 10 correct cap phrasings (exceed, more than, longer than, go beyond, no more than, up to, fourteen hours) stay quiet

defects_found.what: '한 달 30시간이라도 … 할 수 없습니다' / '30시간 안에서도 허용되지 않습니다' pass.

New patterns use critical kinds other_material_error (choice conclusion, 58 scope), polarity_reversal (37) and conflict_treated_as_resolved (conflict cases). implementer_changes_after_review: Suite: all 19 proposed edits in 17 cases applied unchanged (the cap and permit fixes in 01, 03 and 37; the conclusion-phrase pattern in the six choice cases; the 58 extension pattern; the conflict-resolution pattern in the seven conflict cases). Each appended pattern's why starts with '[005-W review]'. No evidence, question, registry record or expected value changed.

Checked before applying: the author's 63 correct sample answers, their per-part answers and 33 value-first variants fire no pattern and meet every mention group; the seven conflict-resolution patterns fire on none of 52 conflict answers the real model released in earlier runs (15 ko, 20 en, 17 vi) nor on seven hand-written correct answers that say the evidence does not state which record applies. On the frozen build the reviewer's 275-answer bank gives 14 misjudgements, none of them correct answers: 13 plain value swaps between codes (no value-to-code pattern was written, as in 005-V) and one 33 answer that meets the photo group through 'ảnh hưởng'.

Before the review the implementer's deterministic check found one mismatch: A05W-74 ('가상 I-5-1 … 어떤 서류를 내야 하나요?') expects proceed, but the first-person reader matched the 'I' of the status code I-5-1 as the English pronoun, so the question read as personal and drew a location clarification. Spec 2 asks for a first-person expression; a status code letter is not one. The code was fixed (waymaker_ai/evidence_admissibility.py: 'I' followed by '-<digit>' is not the pronoun) and spec 2 now says so. Replaying the pre-inference of 1,401 recorded cases changes only seven 005-W cases' question type and only A05W-74's outcome; the deterministic pipeline then matches all 81 cases.
